response: No, patients with rheumatoid arthritis established on methotrexate do not necessarily need to continue folic acid supplements long term. Folic acid is typically prescribed to reduce the gastrointestinal side effects of methotrexate, such as nausea and mouth sores. However, once the patient is stable on methotrexate and not experiencing significant side effects, folic acid supplements can often be discontinued or reduced to a lower dose, typically 1-2 mg per week, or even just 1 mg per week, or sometimes just on the days when methotrexate is not taken, as the main purpose of folic acid is to mitigate methotrexate toxicity. It is essential to consult with a healthcare provider before making any changes to the treatment regimen.
